title: BNCI 2016-002 Emergency Braking during Simulated Driving dataset
description: EEG, EMG and vehicle-dynamics recordings from 15 healthy participants who drove a simulated racing car while closely following a lead vehicle that occasionally braked abruptly. The dataset supports detection of emergency braking intention from brain activity before the behavioral response, using an ERP-based (P300-like) target/non-target paradigm. It is a preprocessed BIDS derivative of the BNCI Horizon 2016-002 dataset, intended for research on driver assistance and neuroergonomics.
methods_description: Participants drove a virtual racing car (TORCS) with a steering wheel and gas/brake pedals, following a lead vehicle at 100 km/h. The lead vehicle decelerated abruptly every 20-40 s, requiring emergency braking. Three 45-minute blocks were recorded with a BrainAmp amplifier (59 EEG channels, plus EMG, EOG and vehicle signals). Signals were filtered, synchronized and resampled to 200 Hz.
